title: Taebong
capsule: Taebong (태봉, 泰封) was a short-lived Korean kingdom of the Later Three Kingdoms period, founded by the rebel monk-warrior Gung Ye (궁예), who had carved out a northern realm from Silla's decaying territories, initially called Hugoguryeo (Later Goguryeo) and then Majin before adopting the name Taebong in 911. Gung Ye established his capital at Cheorwon, professed Buddhism while instituting himself as a Maitreya Buddha figure, and imposed brutal autocracy, executing ministers and family members on fabricated charges. His generals, led by Wang Geon (왕건), staged a coup in 918, deposed and killed Gung Ye, and Wang Geon founded the Goryeo dynasty — which would reunify the Korean peninsula by 936.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of Taebong is moderately known from Korean dynastic histories (Samguk Sagi), but its precise boundary against Silla and Later Baekje fluctuated with military campaigns and is not mapped with precision.
